cd <repo>
git add docs/prfaq-opencode-integration.md docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(opencode): correct 18 review findings in spec and prfaq

Both documents passed through merge review (Cursor Bugbot, GitHub
Copilot, Qodo on PR #534) which found 18 real defects post-merge.
Applied directly after two correction-mission spawns stalled
(confirmed genuinely stuck -- 20+ minutes with zero output-transcript
growth and zero target-file mtime change, unresponsive to two direct
status-check pings -- and were stopped; every fix below had already
been independently verified against real source before the stall, so
applying them directly rather than re-spawning was the faster and
equally rigorous path).

docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex:

- AllocateDelegationForkPropagated's claims' = claims frame conjunct
  was a real defect, not a stylistic choice: a forked session could
  acquire a delegation and still never produce a commit trailer,
  because ResolveCommitAttribution requires its candidate in dom
  claims. Fixed to write claims' = claims (+) {sid? -> claims(witness?)}.
- Same operation had no liveness check on witness?, letting a stale
  pre-restart claim authorize a new delegation. Added the same
  alive/bornEpoch=epoch guard sid? already carried.
- Same operation never required sid? to actually be the forked party,
  making it symmetric with witness? -- a concrete exploit followed
  (JoinRootSession(A) -> ForkSession(B,A) -> ClaimMission(B,M) ->
  AllocateDelegationForkPropagated(A, witness=B) let the PARENT acquire
  a delegation off its CHILD's claim). Added sid?.parent != noParent.
- ForkSession had no liveness check on parentSid?, letting a stale
  parent fork a live child across a restart. Added the same guard.
- HarnessNeutrality was false as worded ("no guard or effect mentions
  harness at all") -- CorroborateSession constrains it directly.
  Restated as the precise property that actually holds: harness is
  preserved/compared-to-itself, never used to select behavior.
- Section Scope and Harness Instantiation both claimed resolve.SessionID
  falls back to a process-tree walk. Verified directly: it does not --
  ETHOS_SESSION env, then a corroborated PID, then an error. Corrected,
  and noted this means ETHOS_SESSION is already the harness-neutral
  integration seam OpenCode needs, with zero new ethos mechanism.
- Harness Instantiation conflated a corroborated CLAUDE_PID with the
  SESSIONID it resolves to via ReadCurrentSession. Corrected to
  distinguish the lookup key from the identity it finds.
- JoinRootSession/ForkSession paragraph claimed forking fires a generic
  session.created with nothing tying parent to child beyond transcript
  copying. Verified via context7 against anomalyco/opencode's
  packages/core/src/session.ts: forking fires a dedicated
  SessionEvent.Forked whose payload carries parentID directly --
  simpler, same-context, no need for the separate CLI/TUI
  context.data.session.root/family lookup for this specific case.
- Worktree-keying section asserted ctx.location.directory is
  "sufficient" for correlation-keying without verification. The V2
  plugin overview describes ctx.location as the plugin INSTANCE's own
  load-time location, not necessarily every event's actual session
  location -- restated as an explicit open question for the next
  pipeline stage, not settled here.
- ResolveCommitAttribution's delegation-trailer case claimed the
  WriteCommitTrailers consistency check was unnecessary "as a direct
  consequence of the delegationOf invariant." Verified directly:
  WriteCommitTrailers only compares the sidecar's own self-reported
  MissionID string, never looks up the actual delegation record.
  Restated as an assumption the model's writers must maintain, not
  something the real reader re-verifies.
- Cited docs/MODERNIZATION_CASE_STUDY.tex, confirmed not to exist
  anywhere in this repo, as evidence for the FailClosedOnAmbiguity
  precedent. Replaced with the real, verified incident: commit
  d3ba3c4 (bead ethos-jawp, PR #412) -- a stale delegation-binding
  sidecar mis-attributing commits, the mirror-image failure shape.
- audit_log.go non-goal claimed "no sidecar fallback for a Tier A
  spawn" without noting a sidecar fallback DOES exist -- it is
  Tier-B-only, confirmed by the function's own comment. Corrected to
  state the real, narrower gap (ethos-f298 unaffected).
- Added a missing \label{sec:opbind} the new cross-reference needed.
- Added a Validation subsection documenting re-verification after
  these corrections: fuzz 0 errors, setsize-1 probcli unchanged
  (286 states/3862 transitions/0 violations), and an honest note that
  the specific flagged setsize-2 invocations were not rerun given
  runtime cost, with reasoning for why none of these corrections would
  be expected to introduce a new violation.

docs/prfaq-opencode-integration.md: the matching corrections --
process-tree-walk removal, PID/session-ID precision, the real
SessionEvent.Forked/parentID mechanism, the real global
$HOME/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<id>/ storage location (not
per-worktree, three instances), the real mission-claim identity-
propagation requirement (ETHOS_SESSION must reach the committing
shell, not just the claim subprocess), the real stderr diagnostic
behavior (not "no channel to report"), the ctx.location open question,
the real ethos-jawp citation (two instances), and an explicit
disclosure that punt-labs/points' built-in-only plugin policy blocks
adopting this integration there as currently designed.

Verified: fuzz 0 errors, probcli setsize-1 clean (286 states, 3862
transitions, 0 violations, 0 deadlocks), pdflatex compiles cleanly to
25 pages, markdownlint 0 issues, make check exits 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -3
